steps.speaker: Old Woman
steps.content: Don't be mad... He's just looking out for you...
The old woman clutches at the bedsheet, tearing at it hysterically while muttering something.

steps.speaker: Old Woman
steps.content: Right, you saw it, didn't you? These are the flowers he brought back specifically... He brought them...
The old woman swings her head back to glare at a hanger with a coat on it. She continues with a slightly menacing expression.

steps.speaker: Old Woman
steps.content: You little punk!

steps.speaker: Old Woman
steps.content: Say something! You... you'd really rather die than give in, huh?!

steps.speaker: Old Woman
steps.content: Can't you all just... get along peacefully...

steps.speaker: Old Woman
steps.content: Just get along while you...
The old woman goes quiet suddenly, sitting on the bed with a blank expression.
Tears well up in her bleary eyes, streaming down her wrinkled face.
Moore's hand rests on the observation window without turning around.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: She is the survivor of a minor dark web attack many years ago.
The creaks of a metal cart interrupt Moore's account.
A nurse pushes a medicine cart to the door of the ward. Upon seeing Moore, she speeds up as if finding her savior.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Moore, you're finally here. Ms. Henie hasn't been well these past few days. She won't take her medicine or listen to us.

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Please, we're counting on you. We don't know what else to do with her...

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Ah, I get it now.
Moore takes the medicine, pushes open the door, and walks into the ward.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Granny Henie, I've come to see you.

steps.speaker: Henie
steps.content: ...Who are you?!
The old woman looks up hopefully, but shrinks back warily upon seeing who it is.

steps.speaker: Henie
steps.content: You're not... not my child... Who are you?!

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I'm Moore who lives downstairs, Granny Henie.

steps.speaker: Henie
steps.content: Moore... who...? I don't know you. Where are my kids?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: They'll be back in a while. Why don't you take your medicine first?

steps.speaker: Henie
steps.content: Oh... Oh! Right, they're working late... I need to take my medicine...
The old woman lowers her head, and Moore immediately leans in to bring the medicine close to her mouth.
Suddenly, the old woman looks up and shoves Moore's hand off.

steps.speaker: Henie
steps.content: No! They wouldn't come here! ...Who are you? Why are you lying to me?!
The old woman keeps swinging her arms. Moore's outstretched arm turns red from the blows, and the pills are spilled all over the floor.

steps.speaker: Henie
steps.content: Where am I? I want to go home... I want to go home! Where are my kids?!
The old woman cries out. Moore simply embraces her gently, patting her back and soothing her softly.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: It's okay, don't be afraid... I'm here.
The violent outburst of emotions drains the old woman's energy. Soon, she stops struggling and calms down in Moore's embrace.
Moore brings the medicine to the old woman's lips skillfully, guiding her to take it, then gently wipes the tears off her face.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Heh, do we look like we're related?
She smiles back at you, but her gaze never meets yours.
For a long time, Moore just sits by the bed, quietly watching the old woman sleep.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: ...Her name is Henie. She was only a neighbor.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: You know, I've been on my own for so many years. I taught myself programming and kept honing my skills. I could support myself by doing odd jobs online since I was very young. The small apartment I purchased was nice and safe. I had everything I needed without stepping out of my home.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: But over time, I started having some small problems... Because I was too obsessed with the internet and data, I often forgot to eat and turned into a night owl. Not only did my vision deteriorate, but I also frequently fainted from low blood sugar.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: You see, I got many of my bad habits during those days. Back then, I didn't look anything like the reliable professional I am today.

She smiles and rolls up her sleeves to show you the band-aids all over her arms. They all have different patterns and were probably from by kind colleagues who couldn't stand her clumsy behaviors anymore.
You don't look that reliable now either... You hold back the jest and continue listening to her.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Then, one day, I took on a huge job. After pulling several all-nighters in a row to finish it, I was glad to finally be able to relax and have a good meal.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: But I forgot the takeout on the table had been delivered two days ago. I was too tired to notice the strange taste, and the next thing I knew... I ended up with a serious case of food poisoning.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: That was probably the closest I've come to death. The whole world was spinning... I couldn't even walk straight. In the end, I had only one thought left: Should I crawl out and seek help? Or try to upload my last thoughts to the vast sea of data?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Oh, don't you worry. I'm still alive, see?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Thankfully... the Bruce family next door came banging on my door and shouting to ask if I needed help.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Apparently, they'd been worried about this girl next door who rarely went out. It just so happened they passed by my unit that day and heard the thumping and groaning inside, so they just barged in. Then I was sent to the hospital...

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I think that was the night I became that kid they couldn't leave alone to die. Since then, they've taken me in.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Mrs. Bruce sent samples of the programs I'd written to the university she worked at and got me admitted to the school to continue my studies. After I graduated, Mr. Bruce recommended me for a job at his company to help me integrate into society.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Mrs. Bruce used to take me to school. And after I graduated, Mr. Bruce would drive me between home and work. They were always worried I'd get lost, get hurt, or get abducted if they didn't watch over me.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Granny Henie took care of my meals every day. She woke me up in the morning, cooked lunch for me, and invited me over for dinner in the evening... Her cooking is so good. It's a million times better than the most expensive takeout I've ever ordered.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Hehe, it's all thanks to Granny Henie I'm now so healthy and no longer malnourished.
It's rather uncharacteristic of her to talk so much. As she speaks, a gentle breeze stirs the curtains, letting sunlight fall on her long hair, which makes her expression even warmer and softer.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Actually, the day I got food poisoning was my eighteenth birthday. I only realized it because they asked me during the consultation. I had forgotten about it for years.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: That day, Granny Henie even baked me a small cake upon learning that. Of course, it was more for my eyes at the time.
...Memory? Looking at the skinny, lonely old woman and Moore's desolate expression, you suddenly have an ominous feeling.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Where are the Bruces now?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Yeah... Where are they?
Moore turns her head and looks out the window.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I wish they could come back too. That would cheer Granny Henie up.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Are you saying...

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: After my graduation, Mr. Bruce recommended me to work at his company to help me integrate into society.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Was he investigating the dark web at that time, and got...
The smile remains on her face, but it gradually loses its warmth.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: In N.F. 110, Mr. Bruce died in a car accident. The next day, his wife jumped off the balcony of their apartment.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: That night, the Bruce family's computer malfunctioned and caused a fire. Everything was burned to ashes.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I happened to have just received an important task at that time, so I was... haha... working late.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: When I rushed back, Granny Henie was holding her son's portrait, watching the apartment burn and her daughter-in-law get carried away. By that time, she...

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: She couldn't recognize me anymore.
For the first time, you glimpse something else behind Moore's gentle gaze.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Have you been taking care of her for the four years following the incident?
Moore doesn't answer, just quietly watching the old woman lying in bed.
After a long while, she speaks.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I like commands, information, logic, and feedback. I like work requests and challenges. I explore boundaries and rules when I can, delving into all sorts of inevitabilities and possible ways to manipulate them. I like being a programmer.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: A small living space and a computer are all I need. Since I was very little, after all these years, even now, I have always believed that. It's just that...

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I don't care about the world behind the door, but there's always someone who knocks on that door, lets the sunlight in, and guides me into that light.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I don't care about myself either. I don't even remember my own birthday. But for a few years, there was a family that would celebrate it with me each year, never leaving me alone.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: They took me out of that dark little apartment, led me into society, and helped me gain others' trust and care. Now, I've become a truly reliable person.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: ...But I can no longer go back to that home that was always within reach.
She finally looks up at you.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: A part of me already died on that rainy night in N.F. 110.
Moore turns her gaze back on you, smiling faintly.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: This is why I've been investigating the dark web.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Is there anything else... you want to know?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You don't get to see her very often. I'll leave you two alone.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Don't worry about it. I'm glad you came. Please stay with me a bit longer.
She gives a small smile, still warm and pure as always. But as the sunset falls on her, it reveals a blood-like sorrow.

The old woman beside her suddenly groans and sits up from a possible nightmare. Seeing the two figures next to her, she lets out a shrill scream. Her withered body springs up from the bed, struggling and knocking over the IV bottle as she's about to fall off the bed.
Before she can injure herself, Moore quickly steps in and holds her tightly, protecting her.
The old woman stays held like that as she continues struggling and screaming hysterically.

steps.speaker: Henie
steps.content: Where are you? Where are my kids!! Don't go there. Come back. Come back!!

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: They will be back, Granny Henie, they will. Let's wait for them here, okay?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: It's almost dinner time. I'll wait with you until they're back.
Failing to understand her, the old woman simply continues crying and struggling.

steps.speaker: Henie
steps.content: Give them back to me...!!

Hearing the commotion, the nurses rush in with bandages, sedatives, IV drips, and a helpless and regretful expression. Moore simply holds the old woman tightly with her back turned to you, so you can't see her face.
But nothing can hide the trembling in her shoulders in the sunset. You hear an almost inaudible plea. A plea to you.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I'd like... to stay here a bit longer. Please let me... spend some more time with her.

23:41
MBCC Chief's Office
Moore is staying at the nursing home temporarily. In a way, this is a well-deserved short break for her after the recent period of high-intensity work.
As for you, you're back to the MBCC. The earlier meeting has already yielded some results. Heaps of reports from various departments have piled up on your desk.
You immediately notice the report from the 9th Agency. Upon a quick look, several pieces of key information catch your attention.
"We have identified the area where the dark web server might be located. The investigation is in progress."
"However, the entity behind the dark web has not left further traces. Considerable time is required to pinpoint the server's exact location. There is also a significant manpower shortage..."
Reading the report, you feel an urgent need to talk to the 9th Agency, so you dial their number.

options: It was negligence on my part.

choices.text: It was negligence on my part.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: My apologies. I underestimated the difficulty of the actual search. I'll immediately assign more staff...

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: Don't blame yourself, Chief. All the time you spent on Moore was worth it.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: It was perhaps the best solution for the dark web operation.
You pause to digest your special agent friend's words. A moment passes before you ask.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Because she is capable? Or because she is suspicious?
He smiles noncommittally.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: That's for you to decide.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: We've always kept an eye on those related to the DisCity dark web and have even uncovered spies. Miss Moore hasn't shown any suspicious behavior. She is either truly innocent or so good at hiding that even we cannot detect it.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: You see, the 9th Agency must remain ever-skeptical, but our suspicion doesn't always pan out. If possible, we would also like to set aside our differences and partner with a genuinely outstanding talent.

steps.speaker: 9th Agency Staff
steps.content: So, Chief, this time we want to hear your judgment. After observing her for so long, have you come to a conclusion?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I can't conclude something even you can't determine having only been involved for a matter of days. With so many possibilities, there isn't enough time to verify them one by one...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But I think there's one thing I can and must do now...
You pick up the communication device and dial the adjutant's office.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Nightingale, help me contact someone. Right... It's him... Yes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Please do it as soon as possible.
The call ends and the office is silent again. You ponder quietly in the dimly lit office for several minutes.
Finally, a plan begins to take shape in your mind.

█/█
14:32 MBCC Chief's Office

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Huh? T-treatment?
Moore looks up from her workstation, surprised by what you said.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's right. Ever since that visit to the nursing home, I've been concerned about the condition of Ms. Henie... your neighbor.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's why I reached out to this medical team a few days ago. They've cured many Mania patients in West District after the BR-002 incident last year and have a lot of experience with mental disorders caused by mild Mania.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I've talked to them, and the doctor is quite optimistic about Ms. Henie's condition and has even put forward a specific treatment plan.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Moore, what do you think?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I've worked with this medical team many times. You can trust their skills. You don't need to worry about the treatment costs...

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I... I'm not worried about those things.
Behind Moore's smile, there's a hint of confusion.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Not a day passes that I don't hope Granny Henie can be cured, that she can be normal again and remember me.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: But now that you're telling me that she might actually be cured, I suddenly feel a bit... afraid.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Afraid?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Yes, afraid. Afraid that when Granny Henie regains her senses, she'll find that her kids and her closest family... are already gone.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Is this painful clarity really what she wants?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She lives in a constant nightmare now. Perhaps taking a step forward could offer a chance of relief.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Besides... you're her family too. You can support her to escape this nightmare.
Moore looks at you, and after a moment of silence, she smiles.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: ...Hmm, you're right. How could I have forgotten about this?

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Yeah, I'm Granny Henie's family too.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: I will always be by her side, just like how they helped me in the past. I'll help her and take care of her...
Moore says as if trying to convince herself.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: With your consent, I'll notify the medical team right now.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If we request the transfer today, the surgery can be done tomorrow. The doctor says the postoperative treatment won't take long. If all goes well, Ms. Henie will recall all about you by tomorrow evening.
You say as you hand over a note with the new hospital's address.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You should go and be with her for the surgery tomorrow.
Moore takes it and responds with a warm smile.

steps.speaker: Moore
steps.content: Thank you, Chief.
